Our shared view on AI

Let the bots type.
We’ll keep the judgment.

AI is already a brilliant accelerator: it can draft code, explain the mysterious bits, generate tests, and turn a napkin idea into a prototype. It can also be confidently wrong, insecure, inaccessible, or completely unaware of what users actually need. So our team rule is simple: use the tool, understand the result, and verify before shipping.

01 / Try, then ask

AI should sharpen our skills, not quietly skip the part where we learn to solve the problem.

02 / Review like it’s prod

Tests, security, reliability, accessibility, and human review are still very much on the roadmap.

03 / Build what matters

When code is cheap and abundant, good requirements, product thinking, and maintainable systems become the real craft.

→In 5–10 years: agents will handle more implementation, testing, and deployment. Engineers will spend more time setting guardrails, shaping systems, understanding users, and deciding what is worth building. The future is automated; responsibility is not.
